question: The EU-funded European Raw Materials Alliance (ERMA) recently issued a report entitled ‘Materials for Energy Storage and Conversion: A European Call for Action’1. This report lists a number of current and potential raw materials projects identified through the ERMA investment pipeline.
Among these projects is the Australian company Rafaella Resources (now Pivotal Metals), whose only European projects were the San Finx and the Santa Comba tin and tungsten mines in Galicia.

In 2023, sanctioning procedures were initiated against both mines for illegal discharges of water with heavy metals, leading to the cancellation of mining permits and concessions in Santa Comba and the cancellation of San Finx’s water discharge permit, in addition to a EUR 180 000 fine. Both mines remain closed and are the subject of a number of criminal proceedings connected to pollution and corruption charges. 1.
Is the Commission considering supporting illegal mining operations in Galicia through its investment channels or by granting strategic interest on the basis of the Critical Raw Materials Regulation?
Will the Commission inquire into why ERMA included illegal mining operations in Galicia, whose licences had been withdrawn, as part of its ERMA investment pipeline?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.6.2024) The Commission does not intend to support any illegal activities including illegal mining activities. Any recipient of EU funding must fulfil certain criteria and ensure high standards under the EU and national legislative framework.

Furthermore, applications for strategic projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act1 need to provide evidence of how they comply with the sustainability criterion set out in Article 6(1)(c), which refers to a broad range of social and environmental sustainability aspects. Once granted the status of a strategic project, the project promoter will need to obtain necessary permits for the investments.

The relevant national authorities will further analyse and assess if the project fulfils all the criteria to obtain the needed permit. During the implementation of the project, the promoter will have to update the Commission of any changes related to the sustainability criterion.

The European Raw Materials Alliance2 (ERMA), operating under the European Institute of Innovation and Technology Raw Materials, has evaluated both projects in the past – before the actions taken by the Galicia authority. Neither project have received any service/support from ERMA. Any development of these investment projects is conditioned on meeting all necessary legal requirements.
